input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: Section 17 addresses termination consequences in one direction only: Sparkling must cease use and return/destroy Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes, and on Garman default the license converts to perpetual (p0128). Nothing anywhere in the Agreement obliges Garman to provide post-termination transition assistance or to return Sparkling's data in a usable format, or to certify deletion — Section 4 covers only inbound data conversion, Section 16 escrow covers source code, and the Section 18 survival list contains no exit-assistance provision. This falls short of even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus data export within 30 days), so we insert a preferred-position exit clause as new Section 17(d).

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data return/deletion obligation in Section 17
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an exit clause so that, on any termination or expiry, Garman provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates and returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days before certifying deletion. The Agreement currently has no data return or transition mechanic, which leaves us exposed on exit; we can accept a 90-day assistance period if six months is not workable.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (1) at Sparkling's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates; (2) within thirty (30) calendar days of such expiry or termination, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data in Garman's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (3) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Sparkling in writing.
